events.credibility_reason: The rational-Finsler-chain claim rests only on Wikipedia; the cited page was not read for it.
Withdrawn by the author for a computational error in the derivation of the main results.

why: The statement asks for the minimal area (hemisphere) over all shortcut-free fillings of any topology, so the disk, genus-one, Möbius (self-reverse) and large-genus-with-systole results are cases, and the topology-free lower bounds of Briggs–Wells (≈1.36π) and Chen–Li–Zhong (≈5.357, >5.40 orientable) are bounds on the minimal area that stay below 2π. Chambers's genus-dependent constant is likewise a bound. Züst's local result concerns inscribed Riemannian mass of currents in metric spaces near a hemisphere, a changed question, so variant; the discrete, near-flat, rational-Finsler, closed-surface systolic and minimal-surface-in-S³ events are variants. Müller is withdrawn. Chen–Li–Zhong stays credible: the only objection to its orientable step comes from an AI referee (F8), the Lean build is not digestion (F7), and Theorem 1.1 carries no specific objection. The close call is its AI role: 'used OpenAI language models while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments' does not say that the model produced any argument, construction or case in the result, and 'the authors are responsible for the mathematical content' points the other way, so I answered none rather than assisted.
doubts: Chen–Li–Zhong's AI role could be assisted if 'developing' meant the model supplied parts of the nonlinear-resonance argument; the record cannot settle this. Pith's unanswered frequency-mismatch objection to Theorem 1.2 was automated and is not a knock-down, but a human should check it; the general bound in Theorem 1.1 would survive regardless. Cossarini's thesis committee is unnamed, so I left it unreviewed. Ambi's genus threshold and systole hypothesis were never read. The frozen wording ('surfaces in Euclidean space') differs from the Riemannian-filling literature; the scopes above hold under either reading.
